text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.

Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.

The game is over. Every killer is out. The town wins. The roles were: Sonnet the citizen, Haiku the officer, Gemma the citizen, Sol the killer, Luna the killer, Terra the doctor, Opus the citizen.

Day 1, Luna claimed Sol had asked her to answer for him, and Sonnet called that a made-up deflection. Luna was voted out that day, and her last words named Sol as her partner. On Night 2 Sonnet was killed, and on Day 2 Haiku claimed officer and named Sol. Opus pushed the town to vote Haiku out, a read he later called a mistake, and Haiku's card showed officer after he was gone. On Day 3 Sol claimed doctor, Terra contradicted him, and Sol was voted out, so the town won.
